final_report.root_cause: The rate service process (hotel-reserv-rate) crashes on startup because it encounters a MongoDB authorization failure while initializing application data. The container successfully reaches the mongodb-rate service but either has no DB credentials configured (missing Secret/env) or has invalid credentials/insufficient MongoDB user permissions for the rate-db database. The application treats this auth error as fatal and exits with code 1, causing Kubernetes to put the pod into CrashLoopBackOff.
affected_resources: MongoDB database: rate-db (logical resource accessed by the app)
final_report.evidence_summary: Priority #1 investigation (completed) captured container termination state and application logs showing: successful DB session establishment ('New session successfull...') followed immediately by a fatal MongoDB authorization error: "not authorized on rate-db to execute command { count: \"inventory\", ... }". kubectl describe shows container Last State=Terminated (Exit Code=1) and CrashLoopBackOff/back-off restart events. Priority #2 inspection of the pod spec shows the container environment exposes only JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO and no explicit DB host/port/credentials env vars, while the mongodb-rate Service exists and has endpoints, indicating network/service presence but missing or incorrect credential configuration on the application side.
final_report.investigation_summary: Higher-priority (P1) app-level logs were retrieved and show the app connects to MongoDB but immediately fails authorization during initialization (generating test data) and exits with code 1. This explains the CrashLoopBackOff observed in kubectl describe. A secondary (P2) config/dependency check confirmed the MongoDB service is present and reachable (ClusterIP and endpoint exist), but the pod spec lacks DB connection environment variables or mounts for credentials, consistent with the app using defaults or no credentials and being unauthorized. Lower-priority hypotheses (probes, OOM, node issues, image/entrypoint) were not necessary because the logs and termination reason directly point to an application-level auth failure during startup. Remediation: provide valid DB credentials (or mount the correct Secret/env) and/or adjust MongoDB user permissions for rate-db, and make initialization tolerant of auth failures if appropriate.
